A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoDA research work and provide readable text, equations, tables and figures. V1 ends after its references; v2 retains the main study and adds Appendices A–C. The added appendix is a substantive addition, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: V1 reports original continual-learning experiments on five datasets, component ablations, projection-energy analyses and computational comparisons in Tables 1–6 and Figures 3–6.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds original sensitivity studies, CLIP evaluations, backbone and model-size comparisons, and loss-landscape analyses in its appendices.

M1.justification: The original LoDA procedure remains unchanged, but Appendix C.3 introduces a substantial CLIP adaptation. It combines a frozen CLIP model with a prototypical classifier and a separately LoDA-tuned model trained with an image–text matching loss. Prediction uses weighted score fusion between both models in Eq. C.3.1, extending the original single-backbone inference procedure.

E1.justification: V2 retains the five original downstream datasets and adds UCF101 action classification, Aircraft recognition and Cars recognition in Tables 8–9. These extend the represented tasks and visual categories beyond the original evaluation; changing pretrained backbones is assessed separately under E3.

E2.justification: Tables 8–9 introduce evaluated comparators including CoOp, ZS-CLIP, SimpleCIL, RAPF and PROOF without experience replay. Table 10 adds LAE and HiDe-Prompt, while Table 7 expands the overhead comparison with CODA, SLCA and SSIAT. Original comparison memberships remain intact; Seq-LoRA corresponds to the existing sequential LoRA baseline.

E3.justification: The original settings remain, while new evaluations introduce LAION-400M-pretrained CLIP, alternative initial/incremental class splits, DINO/iBOT initialization, different ViT sizes, rank and hyperparameter sweeps, and two-dimensional loss-plane testing. One new protocol is internally ambiguous: Appendix C.3 specifies a 100-class UCF subset, but Table 8 includes a B100 Inc20 setting.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and merging ablations, v2 adds GAO loss trajectories, broader hyperparameter sensitivity, rank/resource analysis, and comparisons across pretraining methods and model sizes. Figures 11–12 examine both general and isolated update directions in two-dimensional loss landscapes, extending v1's one-dimensional general-direction analysis.

E5.justification: The retained experiments preserve their three-seed averaging and uncertainty entries. Figure 8 extends the existing practice with three-seed means and error bars. No increased run count, new uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence interval or significance test is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their numerical results, while Tables 7–10 and Figures 7–12 add substantial new findings. For example, Table 10 newly reports LoDA last accuracies of 73.66 with DINO and 76.83 with iBOT. An added entry is inconsistent: Table 7 gives VPT-NSP 75.69 versus 76.13 in retained Table 6 under the same stated 20S-ImageNetR setting.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds proofs of Theorems 3.1 and 3.3 and a derivation of the general-subspace solution in Eq. 4. Section B.4 additionally develops a gradient-alignment expansion and a future-loss bound using a newly stated gradient-cone assumption with bounded residual. These substantially expand the formal analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about projection energy, dual-subspace LoDA, GAO, closed-form recalibration and empirical superiority. The appendix adds evidence and extensions without revising those headline claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations of hyperparameter failure regimes, rank saturation and the larger gains on smaller models. Appendix B.4 connects GAO's resistance to future interference to a conditional gradient-cone model, while C.3 discusses preservation of pretrained CLIP representations. These extend v1's existing sharing-versus-isolation interpretation.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 newly documents feature caching, zero initialization, cumulative-statistic updates and disabling the isolated branch on the first task. Appendix C.3 explains CLIP prototype construction and score fusion. The existing optimizer, training budget and hardware disclosures remain; the new fusion coefficient alpha is not assigned a value.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the original novelty positioning remain unchanged. The appendix adds focused positioning against CLIP prompt learning, head adaptation and feature replay, with additional references for CLIP, SimpleCIL, RAPF, PROOF, self-supervised pretraining and the new datasets.

P1.justification: The existing narrative, section order, abstract and conclusion are retained. V2 organizes new material into Appendices A–C, repairs the unresolved 'Appx.??' reference to 'Appx.B.2', and updates the date. There is no extensive rewriting or reorganization of the existing text.

P2.justification: V2 adds the staged Algorithm 1 display, Tables 7–10 and Figures 7–12, including sensitivity plots, model-size comparisons and loss-landscape panels. Existing main-text displays are largely retained; Figure 4 corrects update labels to include w_G. The new visual evidence substantially expands the presentation.

improvement.justification: Appendices A–C address substantial gaps in v1 by supplying missing derivations, making the training pipeline explicit, and extending limited sensitivity and backbone evidence with controlled analyses. This materially improves the method's inspectability and empirical support. New reporting inconsistencies remain, including the VPT-NSP discrepancy between Tables 6–7 and the UCF split mismatch, and the GAO argument is conditional on its cone assumption. These limitations temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial gains in explanation and validation.
